replacements.text: feat(acceptance-criteria): the attack panel files coverage gaps under one rule only [9k9.405.14]
two overlapping criteria-standard rules ask different questions

The acceptance-criteria standard has a coverage rule that asks whether each commitment has a criterion. Another rule opened with a sentence that held this question. Its reviewer filed coverage gaps under that rule. The rule now asks only what check each criterion names. On the corrected control document, 9 of 10 panel runs return an empty report, up from 2 of 10. All 10 runs on the defective document still object to the planted criterion.
The run records behind the numbers are in an untracked scratch directory on the author's machine.
Every existing attack record's fingerprint changes. The emitted prompt includes the rule text.
The panel stops catching a defect it caught before.
Every spec attacked with the deployed standard, in every project.
All 10 runs on the defective document still objected to the planted criterion under the planted rule.
The gain on the control document is noise.
The owner, who would believe the panel is quieter than it is.
Ten runs per document used the same model and effort. The one remaining control objection cites a flaw present in both document versions.
The `verification-contract` rule opened with a sentence that held the coverage rule's question. It now judges each criterion's own check. It sends the other question to coverage.
The attack skill's table gains a column naming what each reviewer reads. That unit decides who owns a rule.

The `verification-contract` rule opened by saying that every material commitment has a feasible check. That sentence holds the coverage rule's question. The reviewer that owns `verification-contract` filed coverage gaps under it. On the pilot's second case, 18 of 20 runs raised such objections under the rule as it was.

Each attack-panel reviewer is defined by the unit it reads. One reads a single criterion on its own shape. One reads the set against the document's promises. One reads the set against itself. One asks a single criterion what it leaves untested. The unit decides which reviewer owns a rule. Two reviewers may share ground when one asks about a criterion and the other about the set.

The measurement used the pilot's second case. The case is a realistic document of eight criteria with one planted defect and a corrected control. Ten fresh runs per document read prompts emitted from each standard version. Before and after the change, 10 of 10 defective runs objected to the planted criterion under the planted rule. 1 of 10 defective runs objected elsewhere, down from 10 of 10. 9 of 10 control runs returned an empty report, up from 2 of 10. The one remaining control objection cites a contradiction present in both test-document versions.

No reviewer prompt changed. No existing attack record is reopened. The record check binds to the document's revision and never to the rule text. Other sentences in the attack skill were shortened to keep its body under the size cap.
The `verification-contract` rule judges whether each criterion names a feasible and complete check. It sends the question of whether a commitment has a criterion to coverage.
The attack skill states the unit each reviewer reads beside its reviewer table.
At least 8 of 10 control runs come back empty. At least 8 of 10 defective runs object to the planted criterion.

A rule in the acceptance-criteria standard opened with a sentence that held the coverage rule's question. Its reviewer filed coverage gaps under that rule. On the corrected control document, only 2 of 10 runs came back empty.

The verification-contract rule now judges the check each criterion names. The coverage rule still asks whether a commitment has a criterion. The attack skill's reviewer table names what each reviewer reads. That unit decides who owns a rule.
`make ci` exits 0. On the pilot's second case, ten runs per document produced an empty control report in 9 of 10 runs. All 10 runs detected the planted defect. One prose review round came back clean.

questions.question: Please add a separate Heads-up row for the remaining control objection: it cites a contradiction present in both document versions.
